items:
The armature core should be inspected , particularly for evidences of hot 
 spots or damaged punching. if such damage is observed , this requires very 
 careful and expert repair.

If the core is in need of painting , all surfaces should be cleaned and 
 punching sprayed with general electric epoxy paint the inside of the 
 generator should be checked for evidences of oil which would indicate oil 
 leakage past the oil deflectors

sections.text:
No attempt to grind or repair core damage should be under taken except by a man
who has had previous training . an index perienced man can easily cause
additional damage . and result in a core burnout.

items:
Inspect the ends of the armature winding for deposits of oil and evidences of
 corona discharge , or mechanical damage such as vibration , chafing , loose
 block and ties etc.

If cleaning is necessary , inspect the winding and insulation care fully after
 ward. under ordinary conditions. it should not be necessary to repaint the
 end winding more frequently than once in fire years. to repaint the end
 winding, it is recommended that general electric epoxy paint be sprayed on
 after the winding have been thoroughly cleaned and dried

In
 many cases the cleaning fluids may be applied to the winding by means of a
 spray as an alternative to the use of brushes or clothes .

The
 spray nozzle should be held close to the work so as to obtain the greatest
 benefit from the cleaning fluid .

Two
 or three application of the cleaning fluid may be necessary depending upon
 the amount of oil and dust and after each application , the parts should
 be wiped dry .

In
 case hand scraping of parts is necessary , wooden sticks should be used
 instead of metal scrapers to avoid damaging the insulation .

After
 the winding have been thoroughly cleaned , a finish coat of varnish may be
 applied , if necessary . the varnish may be sprayed while observing every
 precaution tow in imize fire hazard . spray a small test area first to be
 sure that the cleaned area provides a good bonding surface for the varnish
 . all insulating varnishes have a low flash point and ighition may be
 caused by a spark .

sections.text: Procedure for Measuring Shaft to Ground Voltage

items:
The voltmeter or oscilloscope
 should be connected solidly to ground on one terminal ; the other terminal
 to an insulation probe containing a metal - graphite or bronze brush. To
 read shaft voltage , press the probe firmly against the shaft at a point
 adjacent to the grounding brush assembly, but preferably not in the track
 of the grounding brush

The DC component of shaft
 -to-ground voltage is usually below 10 volts, and this DC component is not
 greatly affected by the type of meter which is used. Be sure to connect the
 meter to get an up- scale reading.

The AC component ( or
 peak-to-peak voltage ) is of greatest interest . if the true peak -to -peak
 voltage is 10 volts or less, the indication is that the grounding brush
 assembly is functioning satisfactorily . A peak-to-peak voltage above 10
 volts indicates that maintenance is required.

sections.text:
In general, filters should be cleaned when the pressure drop across the
 filter bank reaches 0.25 inches W.G. However, this figure may vary from
 installation to installation, depending upon the velocities encountered and
 upon the type of dust and dirt being removed from the air stream, and the
 original design conditions.

Under ordinary conditions, far - air filters may be readily cleaned with
 water . A garden hose with pressure nozzel and water pressure of 30 to 40
 psig is satisfactory. Higher pressures are desirable although pressures as
 low as 15 to 20 psig may be used but with less satisfacory results. Hot
 water will speed up the cleaning operation . A nozzle with hose adaptor is
 preferable to an ordinary pressure nozzle .

The stream of water should be directed to the dirty side of the filter so
 that the full energy of the water jet will break the dirt mass loose from
 the media and surplus water will flush the loosened dirt out through the
 herringbone - crimped channels .

When dirt loads are heavy or tenacious, or where a considerable number of
 filters are involved and economy demands a faster cleaning operation, the
 filters should be presoaked in an alkaline cleaning solution. Recommendation
 of the exact material to use should be obtained from the manufacturers of
 cleaning products. Typical alkaline cleaners are

Three generally
 satisfactory, inexpensive dry alkaline materials are turco no. 16, oakite
 penetrant and kelite super S. From 2 to 4 oz. Of this material should be
 used per gallon of water

Prepared alkaline solvents are more expensive than dry compounds, and 
 usually cannot be justified except for removing contaminants having a large 
 percentage of tenacious, greasy substances .

Caution 
 : All
 of the alkaline solution should be thoroughly washed out of the filters with
 fresh water

items:
It is often economical to purchase spare filters for
 installation when the dirty filters are removed for servicing.

It is not generally necessary to clean a Far-Air filter 
 so thoroughly that the bright electroplated surface of the screen media is 
 exposed. Alight residual film of discolored oil in no way changes the 
 filter's performance after it has been reoiled

It may be necessary to front-wash and back - wash
 filters that have heavy dirt and lint loads . It is not necessary to
 wash out the last traces of lint which seem to float within the media .
 However , if a large quantity of dirty lint is permitted to accumulate
 the filters may have to be oiled periodically in a highly alkaline
 solution to remove it .

The condition of the felt on the filter holding frames
 should be checked whenever a filter panel is removed, and repairs made
 when necessary .

A draft gauge installed to measure the resistance
 across an air filter bank best indicates when the filters need cleaning
 .

Air filter maintenance organization using far - air
 automatic or manual air filter cleaning and oiling equipment often can
 do better job more economically than the user. Check with your far - air
 representative for the name of a reputable service company in your area
 .

A resistance temperature detector (RTD) is a resistance element , usually made of copper, and adjusted to 10
 ohms at 25 C. Operation of the RTD is based on the principle that the 
 electrical resistance of a metallic conductor varies linearly with its

rows:
Fig. 
 7 Resistance temperature curve of
copper RTD (10 ohms at 25 C )

sections.text:
The RTD and its associated equipment is designed for use with generators, transformers, and other apparatus to determine winding, gas, and liquid
temperatures. The equipment consist of two parts : the switchboard equipment
which usually includes a temperature meter, test resistor, transformer switch,
and leads: and the machine equipment which usually includes the resistance
temperature detectors, leads, and terminal block with grounding connections.

A test resistance is usually provided for periodically checking the
calibration of the temperature meter. Test resistance has value of resistance
of 11.73 ohms, which corresponds to the resistance of a detector at temperature
of 70 C. A transfer switch is used to connect the temperature meter to any one
of several detectors in the machince. The design is such that the contacts are
opened and closed in proper sequence when transferring from one detector to
another. Another position connects to the calibrated test resistor to check the
temperature meter at the 70-degree point. The construction of RTD'S is shown in
Fig. 6. Each detector has three leads designated as A,B and C the resistance of
the element itself is the total resistance from A to B or A to C minus the lead
resistance B to C.

The magnetic flux path of an ac generator may be sufficiently
non-uniform to cause a small ac voltage to be induced in the circuit ( one turn
1oop ) made up of the generator shaft, bearings and the generator casing. Even
though this induced voltage is small, it could cause a large ac current to flow
if some insulation were not inserted in the circuit if the current were allowed
to flow, it would cause pitting of the bearings the circuit is opened by
insulating the collector end bearing .

The insulation may be checked by the following method use a 0-200 amps-low
impedance ac ammeter with a non-metallic contact, such as a carbon brush to
connect one side of the ammeter to the shaft. Connect the other side the ammeter
to the casing to obtain a measure of the current that might flow with on bearing
insulation present . Disconnect the ammeter from the casing and connect it to
the test terminal of the end shield. if, in this case, the ammeter indicates
even a small current flow, the insulation is not satisfactory and must be
replaced or repaired .

Other units with end shield bearing or pedestal type bearing do not have
means of making electrical contact with the bearing inner liner . on these units
the insulation between the bearing inner and outer ring should be check at
installation and when the unit is shutdown for major inspection . the procedure
for checking bearing insulation is as follows:

The bearing should be replaced or repaired when the resistance across
the bearing insulation measures less than 10,000 ohms.

items: Remove bearing cap at collector end .

Lift the rotor slightly at the collector end , to clear the bearing
using a shaft jacking device as shown in instructions "Assembly and
disassembly of rotor" found elsewhere in the manual . take care not to
damage the oil deflectors .

Using a high resistance ( at least 5000 ohms per volt ) volt -ohm
meter or vacuum tube volt-ohm meter , measure the resistance across the
insulation between the bearing inner and outer rings.

The insulation resistance should be 100,000 ohms or more ; however , a
minimum of 10,000 ohms may be considered satisfactory.

If the resistance across the bearing insulation measures less than
10,000 ohms, remove the upper and lower bearing halves . as before , measure the
resistance across the insulation between the inner and outer rings of the
bearings halves .

The bearing should be replaced or repaired when the resistance across
the bearing insulation measures less than 10,000 ohms.

Shaft - grounding
brushes are supplied on turbine generator units to prevent damage to bearings by
electrical discharge through the oil films.
Shaft - to - ground
voltage occur and turbine - generator or shaft in two ways :
Charge

On units
 with static excitation systems the out put of the three - phase full
 wave bridge rectifiers is not pure DC but contains a 360 hertz ripple of
 appreciable magnitude .
Shaft - grounding
 brushes provide a low - impedance path to ground so that :

Build up of electrostatic voltage

Current flow due to static

 bearings .
Procedure for Measuring Shaft to Ground Voltage
The voltmeter or oscilloscope
 should be connected solidly to ground on one terminal ; the other terminal
 to an insulation probe containing a metal - graphite or bronze brush. To
 read shaft voltage , press the probe firmly against the shaft at a point
 adjacent to the grounding brush assembly, but preferably not in the track
 of the grounding brush
The DC component of shaft
 -to-ground voltage is usually below 10 volts, and this DC component is not
 greatly affected by the type of meter which is used. Be sure to connect the
 meter to get an up- scale reading.
The AC component ( or
 peak-to-peak voltage ) is of greatest interest . if the true peak -to -peak
 voltage is 10 volts or less, the indication is that the grounding brush
 assembly is functioning satisfactorily . A peak-to-peak voltage above 10
 volts indicates that maintenance is required.

Far
- Air Filters
When to Clean
In general, filters should be cleaned when the pressure drop across the
 filter bank reaches 0.25 inches W.G. However, this figure may vary from
 installation to installation, depending upon the velocities encountered and
 upon the type of dust and dirt being removed from the air stream, and the
 original design conditions.
How
 to Clean
Under ordinary conditions, far - air filters may be readily cleaned with
 water . A garden hose with pressure nozzel and water pressure of 30 to 40
 psig is satisfactory. Higher pressures are desirable although pressures as
 low as 15 to 20 psig may be used but with less satisfacory results. Hot
 water will speed up the cleaning operation . A nozzle with hose adaptor is
 preferable to an ordinary pressure nozzle .
The stream of water should be directed to the dirty side of the filter so
 that the full energy of the water jet will break the dirt mass loose from
 the media and surplus water will flush the loosened dirt out through the
 herringbone - crimped channels .
Alkaline Cleaning Materials
When dirt loads are heavy or tenacious, or where a considerable number of
 filters are involved and economy demands a faster cleaning operation, the
 filters should be presoaked in an alkaline cleaning solution. Recommendation
 of the exact material to use should be obtained from the manufacturers of
 cleaning products. Typical alkaline cleaners are
Dry
 Compounds
Three generally
 satisfactory, inexpensive dry alkaline materials are turco no. 16, oakite
 penetrant and kelite super S. From 2 to 4 oz. Of this material should be
 used per gallon of water
SOLVENTS:
Prepared alkaline solvents are more expensive than dry compounds, and 
 usually cannot be justified except for removing contaminants having a large 
 percentage of tenacious, greasy substances .
Caution 
 : All
 of the alkaline solution should be thoroughly washed out of the filters with
 fresh water
It is often economical to purchase spare filters for
 installation when the dirty filters are removed for servicing.
It is not generally necessary to clean a Far-Air filter 
 so thoroughly that the bright electroplated surface of the screen media is 
 exposed. Alight residual film of discolored oil in no way changes the 
 filter's performance after it has been reoiled
It may be necessary to front-wash and back - wash
 filters that have heavy dirt and lint loads . It is not necessary to
 wash out the last traces of lint which seem to float within the media .
 However , if a large quantity of dirty lint is permitted to accumulate
 the filters may have to be oiled periodically in a highly alkaline
 solution to remove it .
The condition of the felt on the filter holding frames
 should be checked whenever a filter panel is removed, and repairs made
 when necessary .
A draft gauge installed to measure the resistance
 across an air filter bank best indicates when the filters need cleaning
 .
Air filter maintenance organization using far - air
 automatic or manual air filter cleaning and oiling equipment often can
 do better job more economically than the user. Check with your far - air
 representative for the name of a reputable service company in your area

Resistance Temperature Detectors ( R.T.D )
Description
A resistance temperature detector (RTD) is a resistance element , usually made of copper, and adjusted to 10
 ohms at 25 C. Operation of the RTD is based on the principle that the 
 electrical resistance of a metallic conductor varies linearly with its
temperature ( See Fig. 7 )
Fig. 
 7 Resistance temperature curve of
copper RTD (10 ohms at 25 C )
Application
The RTD and its associated equipment is designed for use with generators, transformers, and other apparatus to determine winding, gas, and liquid
temperatures. The equipment consist of two parts : the switchboard equipment
which usually includes a temperature meter, test resistor, transformer switch,
and leads: and the machine equipment which usually includes the resistance
temperature detectors, leads, and terminal block with grounding connections.
Tests
A test resistance is usually provided for periodically checking the
calibration of the temperature meter. Test resistance has value of resistance
of 11.73 ohms, which corresponds to the resistance of a detector at temperature
of 70 C. A transfer switch is used to connect the temperature meter to any one
of several detectors in the machince. The design is such that the contacts are
opened and closed in proper sequence when transferring from one detector to
another. Another position connects to the calibrated test resistor to check the
temperature meter at the 70-degree point. The construction of RTD'S is shown in
Fig. 6. Each detector has three leads designated as A,B and C the resistance of
the element itself is the total resistance from A to B or A to C minus the lead
resistance B to C.
Shaft bearing insulation
The magnetic flux path of an ac generator may be sufficiently
non-uniform to cause a small ac voltage to be induced in the circuit ( one turn
1oop ) made up of the generator shaft, bearings and the generator casing. Even
though this induced voltage is small, it could cause a large ac current to flow
if some insulation were not inserted in the circuit if the current were allowed
to flow, it would cause pitting of the bearings the circuit is opened by
insulating the collector end bearing .
Test
The insulation may be checked by the following method use a 0-200 amps-low
impedance ac ammeter with a non-metallic contact, such as a carbon brush to
connect one side of the ammeter to the shaft. Connect the other side the ammeter
to the casing to obtain a measure of the current that might flow with on bearing
insulation present . Disconnect the ammeter from the casing and connect it to
the test terminal of the end shield. if, in this case, the ammeter indicates
even a small current flow, the insulation is not satisfactory and must be
replaced or repaired .
Other units with end shield bearing or pedestal type bearing do not have
means of making electrical contact with the bearing inner liner . on these units
the insulation between the bearing inner and outer ring should be check at
installation and when the unit is shutdown for major inspection . the procedure
for checking bearing insulation is as follows:
The bearing should be replaced or repaired when the resistance across
the bearing insulation measures less than 10,000 ohms.
Remove bearing cap at collector end .
Lift the rotor slightly at the collector end , to clear the bearing
using a shaft jacking device as shown in instructions "Assembly and
disassembly of rotor" found elsewhere in the manual . take care not to
damage the oil deflectors .
Using a high resistance ( at least 5000 ohms per volt ) volt -ohm
meter or vacuum tube volt-ohm meter , measure the resistance across the
insulation between the bearing inner and outer rings.
The insulation resistance should be 100,000 ohms or more ; however , a
minimum of 10,000 ohms may be considered satisfactory.
If the resistance across the bearing insulation measures less than
10,000 ohms, remove the upper and lower bearing halves . as before , measure the
resistance across the insulation between the inner and outer rings of the
bearings halves .
The bearing should be replaced or repaired when the resistance across
the bearing insulation measures less than 10,000 ohms.
